solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work in that? Maybe if you're like Fred Astaire!

definitions.text: Work in that? Maybe if you're like Fred Astaire!

parts.words: Work in that? Maybe if you're like Fred Astaire!
parts.note: Fred Astaire danced and sang in formal evening dress, famously in a 1935 film named after his tall silk headwear, so a performer like him works wearing it

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a dancer in the style of Fred Astaire might wear on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Astaire's 1935 film and its song 'Top Hat, White Tie and Tails' made the tall silk hat his trademark, so the whole clue points to his working headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire's signature costume piece was the tall formal silk hat he danced in.

clue.text: Propositions to rebuild rest home

indicators.note: rebuilding a structure puts its parts together afresh, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plans are proposed for reconstructing a care home for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges RESTHOME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics and logic a proposition to be proved is a theorem; the plural matches.

clue.text: Holiness and compassion swamping hate ultimately

indicators.note: to swamp is to engulf, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: compassion means pity

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word hate

explanation.surface: A pious virtue pairs with mercy so strongly that it overwhelms hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of 'hate', and 'swamping' puts it inside PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, a synonym for holiness in the sense of godly reverence.

clue.text: Criticises a levy in speech

indicators.note: said out loud, the phrase from the clue sounds like a single word

parts.note: a levy is a tax, so these words give A TAX

explanation.surface: Someone complains, out loud, about a new charge being imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says A TAX, spoken, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack someone verbally is to criticise them harshly, so the verbs match in tense and person.

clue.text: Positioned in front of the boat, I will wave

indicators.note: being positioned in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the bow is the forward end of a ship
I will contracts to I'LL

explanation.surface: A sailor standing at the prow promises to wave goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of the boat' reads as where the speaker stands, but it is the container that 'Positioned in' opens; 'I will' is contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a large rolling wave of the sea, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Innocent and genuine in coming to the fore

indicators.note: the two-letter word in, found within the next word, is brought to the front

explanation.surface: Someone guileless and sincere is finally getting noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in coming to the fore' takes the IN from inside GENUINE and puts it at the start: IN + GENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role; the noun matches 'Innocent' used as a noun.

clue.text: New lad in team given protection outside?

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the side is handed protective gear to wear over his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LADINTEAM. The definition is cryptic: a laminated card has a protective plastic coating on its outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminating covers something in a thin protective film, so a laminated object has been given an outer shield.

clue.text: To go courting and study is awkward

parts.note: to woo is to court someone
a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: Combining romance with homework makes for clumsy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden describes stiff, stilted, ungainly behaviour, so it means awkward.

clue.text: Fellows into stupid diet? There follows a mental disorder

indicators.note: says the last piece comes after what has been built so far
into says one piece goes inside the other
stupid suggests something muddled, so the letters of the word diet are scrambled

parts.note: fellows are men

explanation.surface: A foolish diet for men leads to a psychological illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' scrambles the diet into DETI, which 'into' opens for the fellows; 'There follows' tacks on the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a progressive decline in memory and reasoning, classed as a mental disorder.

clue.text: Notice vehicle with building material moving forward

parts.note: an advert or ad is a public notice
a van is a vehicle
cement is a building material

explanation.surface: A sign shows a lorry carrying mortar travelling onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement is progress or promotion, the act of going forward.

clue.text: Meat in school, first day of lessons?

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
Monday, abbreviated MON, starts the school week

explanation.surface: A school dinner of meat served on the opening day of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a classroom here but a group of whales, a GAM. Gammon is cured ham, a British cut of pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is cured or smoked ham from the hind leg of a pig, a type of meat.

clue.text: Little woman entertaining king's soldiers

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A small woman hosts a monarch's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts R inside AMY, the youngest sister in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large body of soldiers, a collective noun for them.

clue.text: One wanting religious liberty? Witches aren't different

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

indicators.note: different suggests a changed form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Witches insist they are not unusual and simply want freedom to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges AREN'T to ANTER. Covenanters were 17th-century Scottish Presbyterians who signed covenants defending their form of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Covenanters fought for the freedom of their Presbyterian church against royal control.

clue.text: MP and minister on fiddle — to result in this?

definitions.text: MP and minister on fiddle — to result in this?

indicators.note: to fiddle is to tamper or meddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians caught cheating might end up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' rearranges MP and MINISTERON; the whole clue also says where corrupt politicians on the fiddle (cheating) end up.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisonment is the jail sentence that fraud by politicians could lead to.

clue.text: One large town overcome by decay in a style that doesn't suit it?

definitions.text: a style that doesn't suit it?

indicators.note: in a down clue being overcome by something puts it on top, so it comes first

parts.note: rust is a form of decay
the Roman numeral I is one
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A big town falls into decline and ends up looking inappropriately countrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' puts RUST above I and CITY in the down entry. Rustic style is countrified, unsuited to a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusticity is a rural, countrified character, which would be out of keeping with a big town.

clue.text: Goddesses collecting equipment for ships

indicators.note: collecting something means gathering it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Fates are the three goddesses of destiny in Greek myth
a rig is equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Divine beings gather gear needed for a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' has the goddesses of destiny gather the equipment inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigates are warships, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Old ploughmen as investors in company?

definitions.meaning: jocular reading: those who once held the share, the blade of a plough
people who own stakes in a business

explanation.surface: Retired farm workers turn out to be investing in a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: A share is the cutting blade of a plough, so the first sense is a humorous one; 'as' joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Shareholders own portions of a company's stock, making them its investors.

clue.text: Tot hanging around this place gets stuck

indicators.note: hanging around something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add
here means this place

explanation.surface: A toddler loitering nearby ends up trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but means sum up; 'hanging around' makes the sum wrap this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhered means clung or stuck fast, past tense like stuck.

clue.text: Extraordinary old fellow, one from former dynasty

parts.note: over the top, OTT, means extreme or outlandish
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A remarkable elderly man turns out to descend from an ancient royal line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman dynasty ruled the Turkish empire for six centuries, so an Ottoman is a member of it.

clue.text: Maybe Ra is celebrated, with party being set up

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it, so sung means celebrated

indicators.note: in a down clue being set up means turned upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity is honoured at a party being organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being set up' turns DO into OD in this down entry. 'Maybe' marks Ra as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ra was the ancient Egyptian god of the sun, an example of such a deity.

clue.text: Penalty kick is hard, guys admitted

indicators.note: being admitted means let in, so these pieces go inside the first

parts.note: a punt is a kick of a dropped ball
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
guys are men

explanation.surface: A penalty kick is tough, the lads confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penalty kick' reads as one football phrase but splits into definition and wordplay; 'admitted' lets three pieces into the kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment imposed for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Travel beyond river to jump up and down

indicators.note: beyond says this piece comes after the other

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Go past the river and leap about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' sets the travelling after the Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: To pogo is to jump up and down on the spot, as on a pogo stick or at punk gigs.

clue.text: Religious believer in French city a bit confused at the end

indicators.text: a bit confused at the end
indicators.note: only a little of the word is jumbled, at its tail, so its final pair of letters swap round

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A worshipper in a French city gets slightly muddled at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused at the end' swaps the last two letters of PARIS, IS becoming SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism in India, descended from Persian émigrés.

clue.text: One tucks into nasty gruel that's less appealing

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so the first piece sits within the other
nasty suggests something spoiled, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone eats unpleasant porridge that is even less attractive than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges GRUEL to UGLER and 'tucks into' puts I inside. 'tucks into' looks like eating, but it means goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier is the comparative of ugly, meaning less pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Daring, though looking back? There's value in that

indicators.note: says the merit piece goes inside the reversed one just described
looking back means facing the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: yet can mean though or nevertheless
merit is worth or value

explanation.surface: A bold move, though on reflection there's something worthwhile in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' gives TEY, and 'in that' sets the worth inside it; the question mark tempts a definition there, but 'Daring' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness or audacity, a noun matching 'Daring' as a noun.

clue.text: Dull commercials showing nymphs

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
ads are advertisements or commercials

explanation.surface: Boring adverts featuring woodland spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Rock making pleasant sound

indicators.note: a sound is what is heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A stone that makes an agreeable noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' gives the spoken form of NICE, which the rock's name sounds like despite its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock.
